summary: Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships are New Zealand Government scholarships run by Education New Zealand for citizens of eligible Pacific and Asian countries. The tertiary scheme supports full-time undergraduate and postgraduate study at approved institutions in New Zealand, and for some Pacific countries at two Pacific universities. The scholarship covers tuition, a living allowance, an establishment allowance, insurance and airfares, among other components. Scholars must commit to contributing to their country's development for at least two years after study.
eligibility_notes:
Countries: citizens of eligible Pacific countries (Fiji, French Pacific, Kiribati, Naoero, Niue, North Pacific, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu) and eligible Asian countries (Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Nepal, Philippines, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Viet Nam). French Pacific means New Caledonia, French Polynesia and Wallis and Futuna; North Pacific means the Federated States of Micronesia, Palau and the Marshall Islands. Cook Islands scholars use their own scheme run by the Cook Islands Ministry of Education. Tokelau is currently eligible only for the Short Term Training scholarships. Citizens of countries not listed are pointed to other New Zealand scholarships.

Before you start the application you answer an online questionnaire about citizenship, time living in your home country, work experience, whether scholarships are offered to your country, current military service and any previous Manaaki scholarship. You must meet all criteria.

Residence: you must have lived in your home country for the two years before applying. Exceptions are people on a diplomatic assignment for their country (including dependants) and people enrolled in overseas study.

Academic and English: you must meet the academic entry and English requirements of your chosen institution and course. Only subjects listed for your country or region are eligible. English test scores are not needed when you apply; shortlisted applicants must provide them, except for Pacific tertiary study. Scores must be from the last 12 months unless the institution accepts older ones. Accepted tests: IELTS, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic and Cambridge Academic English (Advanced). Indicative minimums (institutions set their own and some are higher): postgraduate IELTS 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0, TOEFL 90 with writing 21, PTE 58 with communicative skills not below 50, Cambridge 176 with no band below 169; undergraduate IELTS 6.0 overall with no band below 5.5, TOEFL 80 with writing 21, PTE 50 with communication skills not below 42, Cambridge 169 with no band below 162. Near-miss preferred candidates may get English training: up to one year in New Zealand for Pacific countries and Timor-Leste, up to one year in the home country for Cambodia, Lao PDR and Indonesia, and up to one semester in New Zealand for all other eligible countries. This is not available for PhD candidates, and the scholarship ceases if the requirement is still not met afterwards.

Contribution: you must contribute to your country's social or economic development for at least two years after finishing study. This is a scholarship condition.

Previous scholars: after a completed tertiary Manaaki scholarship you are not eligible for two years. If the scholarship was terminated, downgraded on academic grounds or you went home without a qualification, you are not eligible for five years. If you withdrew for unforeseen personal reasons or were downgraded on personal grounds, you are not eligible for two years. Termination for inappropriate conduct bars you permanently. Previous English Language Training for Officials or Short Term Training scholars cannot get a tertiary scholarship during their stand-down period (the length is not stated on the page).

Visa: you must qualify for a New Zealand student visa. You apply only after accepting an offer; processing takes two to three months and includes medical tests. If you cannot get a visa, the scholarship is withdrawn.

Subjects: study must align with the recommended subjects for your country or region; applications that do not align strongly are highly unlikely to be considered. PhD applicants should contact possible supervisors early and, by the interview, must have a supervisor or be in active discussion with one.
age_experience_notes: You must be 18 when you sign the letter of offer (Samoa Foundation intake: 17 is allowed when you start). There is no upper age limit, but applicants under 40 are preferred; the selection guidelines say the aim is scholars aged 39 or younger when the scholarship starts. Postgraduate applicants need one year of full-time work (30 or more hours a week) or two years of part-time work (up to 29 hours a week); paid, unpaid or voluntary work counts. This is not needed if you are in the final year of high school when applying, are applying in the academic year right after finishing high school, or are currently employed (paid or unpaid). Preference goes to applicants whose study aligns with their work and who will continue in that sector.
funding_summary: The funder pages name these components: full tuition fees, a living allowance for basic expenses, an establishment allowance for set-up costs, medical insurance in New Zealand and travel insurance, travel to New Zealand at the start and home at the end, trips home for longer awards, tutoring costs if needed, research and thesis help for many postgraduate students, and a reintegration allowance on return. They give no amounts. Length of funding follows the qualification: undergraduate degree 3 to 4 years, postgraduate certificate 6 months, postgraduate diploma 1 year, master's 1 to 2 years, PhD 3.5 years. Scholars studying over 1.6 years can usually make one or two trips home.
programmes_note: Study must be in a recommended subject (sector) for your country or region. The site publishes sector and subject lists per country as search keywords for course catalogues; they are not a guarantee that a course is eligible. In the application you explain how your preferred courses relate to a recommended subject, what skills you want to gain and why they matter for your country's development, and you can save up to three qualification and course preferences. Choose qualifications at a level open to your country and that progress from your highest existing qualification. Not supported (Pacific and Timor-Leste lists): Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) at the University of Canterbury, and Bachelor of Law at Victoria University of Wellington and the University of Auckland. Papua New Guinea: by agreement with the PNG Government, bachelor's degrees that PNG itself offers in medicine (MBBS), law, engineering, primary and secondary teaching and nursing are not offered. Levels per country: postgraduate only for Fiji, French Pacific, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Nepal, Philippines, Thailand and Viet Nam; undergraduate or postgraduate for Kiribati, Naoero, Niue, North Pacific, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu and Timor-Leste. Philippines: 60 percent of places go to Mindanao and the Bangsamoro region, and 40 percent to the Visayas and northern Luzon provinces. Thailand: only one PhD is awarded each year. Malaysia, Timor-Leste and some Pacific lists mark some subjects (such as environmental, maritime and trade law, and disaster or emergency management for Timor-Leste) as postgraduate only.
institutions_note: Approved institutions in New Zealand: Auckland University of Technology, Lincoln University, Massey University, University of Auckland, University of Canterbury, University of Otago, University of Waikato and Victoria University of Wellington (eight universities), plus Southern Institute of Technology and Unitec Institute of Technology (two institutes of technology). Eligible Pacific citizens (Kiribati, Niue, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu) can also choose the University of the South Pacific or Fiji National University. You research each institution's course catalogue yourself and enter up to three preferences. Some funder pages say three institutes of technology but list two.

summary.detail: Undergraduate degree, 3 to 4 years. Open only to some countries: Timor-Leste among the Asian countries, and in the Pacific Kiribati, Naoero, Niue, North Pacific, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu. Fiji and French Pacific are postgraduate only. The Samoa Foundation intake is undergraduate only and needs a 75 percent average in the foundation programme. Study may be in New Zealand, or at a Pacific university for eligible countries.

summary.detail: PhD, 3.5 years. Applicants must be eligible for direct PhD entry and English language training is not supported for PhD candidates. You should contact possible New Zealand supervisors early and, by the interview stage, must have a supervisor or be in active discussion with one. PhD study at a Pacific university is only at the University of the South Pacific or Fiji National University. Thailand: only one PhD is awarded each year. Malaysia and Nepal require direct entry in English. Subjects follow the same recommended sectors as master's study.

Postgraduate certificate (6 months) and postgraduate diploma (1 year) are listed as levels of study alongside the master's and PhD for all eligible countries. The same work experience and recommended-subject rules apply as for other postgraduate study.
summary.source_text: Postgraduate Certificate (6 months); Postgraduate Diploma (1 year)

benefits.conditions: At an approved New Zealand institution, or a Pacific university for eligible Pacific countries. English language training before the main course is available for near-miss preferred candidates (not PhD).

benefits.limit_text: Living allowance for basic living expenses. The funder pages give no amount. Massey University lists NZ$615 per week; Victoria University of Wellington lists NZ$982 every two weeks, paid for all 52 weeks.
benefits.conditions: If you start your study in your home country, the allowance is adjusted for local living costs. The scholarship gives no financial support for family members; those who come with you pay their own travel, visas, insurance and living costs (Victoria University of Wellington).

benefits.limit_text: Establishment allowance for set-up costs such as accommodation, textbooks and study materials. Amounts are not on the funder pages: Massey University lists NZ$3,000; Victoria University of Wellington lists NZ$3,000 on arrival and NZ$1,000 for each later full year.
Medical insurance while in New Zealand, and travel insurance
benefits.conditions: Victoria University of Wellington adds that higher premiums for pre-existing conditions are included.

benefits.limit_text: Travel from your home country to New Zealand at the start and back at the end; scholars studying over 1.6 years can usually take one or two trips home
benefits.conditions: Your institution organises travel and looks after you on arrival. The funder pages give no fare limits.

benefits.limit_text: Tutoring costs if you need extra academic support
benefits.conditions: Massey University mentions up to NZ$1,000 for tutoring; not stated on the funder pages.

benefits.limit_text: Research and thesis costs for many postgraduate students

benefits.conditions: Helps with set-up costs on return. The funder pages give no amount (Massey University lists NZ$1,000).

benefits.limit_text: Visa costs reimbursed with receipts: the visa application fee, the immigration levy and one immigration medical check
benefits.conditions: Not reimbursed: travel to medical or visa appointments, police clearance, courier fees, passport application or renewal, and dependant visa fees. IELTS fees are paid by Education New Zealand for shortlisted applicants from Cambodia, Indonesia, Fiji, French Pacific, Kiribati, Lao PDR, Nauru, North Pacific, Papua New Guinea, Samoa (except Samoa Foundation), Solomon Islands, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu; others pay and are reimbursed on arrival in New Zealand if selected.
The establishment allowance helps with set-up costs including accommodation.

application_steps.title: Check your country, eligibility and recommended subjects
application_steps.detail: Confirm that your country is eligible and which levels it can use, then answer the online eligibility questionnaire. Choose subjects from the recommended list for your country; applications that do not align are highly unlikely to be considered. The site's own steps are: check countries, check criteria, choose a subject, research courses, apply, learn how scholars are selected, preferred candidate steps, and get ready to start.

application_steps.title: Research courses and pick up to three preferences
application_steps.detail: Study the approved institutions' course catalogues and choose qualifications at a level open to your country that progress from your highest qualification. You can save up to three qualification and course preferences in the application. PhD applicants should contact possible supervisors early.

application_steps.title: Apply online in the applicant portal and upload your transcript
application_steps.detail: Pacific and Asian applicants apply through the Manaaki applicant portal. Upload a copy of your academic transcript with the grading scale (not needed for Samoa Foundation applicants). The system may close early for countries with many applications, so apply early. The funder's overview page gives 1 March 2027 to 31 March 2027 for the 2027 tertiary intake; the Samoa Foundation window is 4 August 2026 (midnight) to 4 September 2026 (midday). Massey University gives 1 March 2027 to 10 April 2027.

application_steps.title: Screening and psychometric test
application_steps.detail: Your application is first checked against the eligibility criteria and selection guidelines, and your preferred courses are compared with your country's recommended subjects. You then get an email link to an abstract reasoning and personality test to finish within 10 days. A decision email tells you whether you advance; PhD applicants who advance should contact supervisors if they have not already.

application_steps.title: Detailed assessment, English level and interview
application_steps.detail: Shortlisted applicants are assessed more closely and may be invited to an online video interview (typically May to July). Two interviewers ask six questions in 40 minutes, up to six minutes per question: course choices and national development, motivation, two hypothetical challenge scenarios and one resilience question. Applicants also state their English level.

application_steps.title: Final decision by email
application_steps.detail: You are told whether you are a preferred candidate, on the reserve list or unsuccessful. Selection can take six to ten months from the close of applications, depending on the number of applicants; over 15,000 applications are received each year. Selection looks for strong academic ability, commitment to national development, recommended subjects, work experience, a qualification that progresses from your highest one, return home for at least two years, and a balance of male and female scholars. No individual feedback is given, but you may reapply the next year.

application_steps.title: Preferred candidates apply for admission and an offer of place
application_steps.detail: The preferred institution contacts you. Apply for admission as an international student, saying you are a preferred candidate, and start as soon as you are told. Processing takes about two months for undergraduate and three months for postgraduate applicants. Reply promptly to every message or you may be removed from the preferred list.

application_steps.title: Accept the Scholarship Letter of Offer within 14 days
application_steps.detail: Education New Zealand checks your offer of place and sends a Scholarship Letter of Offer. Read and accept it in the online application system within 14 days; it is a legal contract with the New Zealand Government and acceptance means agreeing to the scholarship conditions. Apply for a student visa only after accepting an offer; it takes two to three months and includes medical tests.

application_steps.title: Prepare, travel, study and return home
application_steps.detail: Attend the pre-departure briefing, read the pre-departure workbook and policy handbook, and meet any prerequisite conditions (valid student visa, extra English training) or the offer is withdrawn. Your institution organises travel and helps on arrival. Attend classes, finish compulsory assessments, sit all exams, make satisfactory progress and keep to the code of conduct from the day you leave home until you arrive home, or the scholarship can be terminated. After study you must contribute to your country's development for at least two years.
